reviews.title: 10 /10 STARS BEST APP EVER
reviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ If I could give Guava Health 10 stars, I absolutely would! 🤩

I came across Guava Health while searching the App Store for a better way to keep track of my health, and I am SO glad I decided to give it a try.

I have lupus along with several other medical issues, so keeping track of everything can get overwhelming. I have consistently forgotten appointments, struggled to remember which doctor I saw and when, and had different health-tracking apps scattered everywhere. Half the time, I would completely forget about those apps and stop tracking altogether.

Guava has changed that for me. 💚 I can finally have so much of my health information in ONE place—appointments, providers, symptoms, medications, medical records, labs, vitals, sleep, activity, and more. I can even connect other health apps, devices, Apple Health, and supported patient portals. I especially love being able to keep a health timeline and prepare information for upcoming doctor appointments. 🩺📊

The amount this app offers for FREE is honestly incredible. There is also Guava Plus for $78/year, which unlocks additional features like deeper health insights and other premium tools. For everything it can do, I personally think the annual subscription is absolutely worth it.

And I don’t even think I’ve scratched the surface of this app’s potential yet! 😂 Every time I explore it, I seem to discover another feature that makes managing my health a little easier.

When you’re dealing with medical issues that are present and affecting your life every day, having everything organized in one place can make such a difference. I’m genuinely excited to continue using Guava and seeing everything I’m able to track and learn over time.

I cannot recommend Guava Health enough. 💚🩺📱 If you’re someone who has multiple doctors, medications, appointments, symptoms, labs, or health conditions to keep track of, this app is absolutely worth checking out.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 10/10 from me!

A way to filter symptoms (could select multiple symptoms) and it tells what days in the past YEAR(S) it occurred regardless of severity.

reviews.title: Brings all your records together. First class app!
reviews.text:
For anyone tracking a complex medical condition, Guava is indispensable. It pulls together your tests and doctors’ notes from all the hospital system, lab company, and medical office portals. You can search, display, and if you want, download your records in clear, organized formats. 

The developers keep updating the app and making it more useful. And they have been very responsive when I’ve asked questions or offered suggestions.

Guava also pulls all your Apple Health information — like workouts — and it lets you log food, meds, and symptoms. There are other apps that do these things, but Guava does a nice job if you want everything together. It says it can find correlations between various health factors; I’ve never found these to be useful. 

Sometimes functions are a little hard to find in the interface, especially download options. But they are there if you look.

The new AI feature can also be helpful if you understand the limits of AI chatbots. You can ask questions about your health records, and the bot can search through them and explain what they mean. As with any chatbot, you should double-check any answer that’s important. 

I pay for the premium service. This lets me upload PDFs of records it can’t automatically connect to, but I do it mainly to support the developers. The free version, I think, offers most of the useful features. 

I don’t write many reviews, but this is a first-class app that many people will find very useful.

reviews.title: Exactly what I need for my health tracking!!!
reviews.text:
This is the best health app I’ve found.

I looked at so many apps trying to find one that will take into account mood, energy level, things I did that day, sleep, sleep conditions, activity, water intake, nutrition, my cycle, symptoms, medications, weather and a few more others. 

This does all of that and more. What’s great is that I don’t have to change my period tracking app or my nutrition tracking app. It pulls data from Apple health, so anything that integrates with Apple health integrates with this. 

I was shocked to see that it’s also HIPAA compliant and it integrates with a lot of doctors apps like MyChart and uses lab data and office visit data too.

Some things are manual to log like your mood your energy level your symptoms but you’d have to do that in any app you choose. 

What’s really great is that if there’s not a category already made for things you want to track then you can add in a custom item to track. I really wanted to track what I did throughout my day so I created categories for things like self-care, home, outings, and relationship.

All that being said, this app uses all of that data and presents you with insights. For instance, it told me that there is a correlation between a higher temperature and how much I sleep. 

Now it doesn’t necessarily tell you what this correlation means if it’s not self-explanatory so for insights about HRV or a subject that is a little bit more complicated and not straightforward. I take a screenshot and I dump it in a ChatGPT and I ask it to analyze for me this system does not use AI to analyze your data.

This is by far the best app I have found to collect all data points and give correlations. I love it so much. It’s so helpful. It’s very insightful and it looks like they have a roadmap to make improvements, even though it’s already so great.

reviews.title: Life changer
reviews.text:
I am so incredibly grateful for this app. I have MCAS along with several other health issues, some which we are still trying to figure out. My MCAS causes severe allergic reactions to nearly everything, even my own menstrual cycle. Although I try to take notes on flares and always take photos, it’s really hard to keep it organized, track patterns, and show an accurate depiction of those patterns to my doctors. 

I just started using Guava and am floored by how comprehensive it is. This is huge for chronic illness folks. They really thought of everything. My favorite features: 
- you can input custom symptoms, all with a scale for severity, and group symptoms together for easy access when logging a flare. 
- The absolute best: you can even upload multiple photos into each symptom log! 
- You can then track/gain insights about even your custom symptoms, which is often not the case with most apps. 
- At the end of each entry there is also free form notes section at the end of the entry. 
- It also has a comprehensive menstrual cycle tracking feature which is huge as lots of us get different issues at various parts of our cycle. 
- It can generate reports for your doctor, and you can even input all your health records to see trends over time. 

I think using this app consistently with chronic illness or mysteriously health issues could lead to big breakthroughs via having more precise data and trends for your doctors.  It makes me feel like I have some sliver of control over this thing that I have felt so powerless in, there’s no greater gift I could ask for. 

Thank you so much to everyone who made this app, and for making it accessible to everyone- I hope that never changes. The basic is free which still has pretty much all features and premium which has the ability to track insights is only $8/mo. A lot of people with chronic illness can’t afford big extra expenses, so the fact that this remains affordable for us is incredible. Every other aspect of the care we have access to essentially boils down to whether we have the $$ for it- so having one free/affordable resource is huge.

reviews.title: I Absolutely Recommend
reviews.text: This app is a life-saver. At least, for me it was. I am a female teen nearing adulthood and I have adhd as well as other problems. I really needed a way to keep track of all my medical information as well as track symptoms and mood and medication and my period, which seemed impossible or extremely hard until I found this app. The free version of Guava has plenty to offer, I can track all of the stuff that I need to and even set reminders to help me make sure to do it. The interface is not complicated in my opinion, you just have to play around with it and explore it a little when you first use it and make it the way you want it to be, then after that logging stuff is super easy. Of course, no app is perfect, but in my opinion, this app is really good especially since it’s free. There is a paid thing that can offer more features but honestly I don’t need it right now plus I don’t have a job for a steady flow of money to pay for it. If you need it or are able to pay for it then i still recommend it to at least support the developers for the amazing free part of the app. I just love this app and I recommend it to anyone. Even if you don’t end up liking it, it won’t cost you anything but a little time to check it out and see how it works for you. Anyways thanks developers for making such an amazing app with most the features free for people like me to access the stuff we need! ❤️Oh yeah, and another thing I love is that it hardly takes up any storage and is compatible with my device, because my device is like 5 years old, a 7th gen iPod Touch which only has a total of 32 GB of storage so that is also a life-saver for me haha.

reviews.title: Sooo much better than Bearable
reviews.text:
I started out using the Bearable app, hoping I could get some good insights about my health and mental health and what factors have impacts on various aspects of my health. Bearable’s data insights were, to put it mildly, useless. They didn’t actually make sense and you couldn’t even compare half of the information you’d been collecting for ages in hopes of getting good, interesting insights. But then I found Guava. I will admit that Bearable’s UI & UX is a bit more visually appealing and intuitive, but Guava reigns supreme in literally every other way. 

You can connect your medical records and Apple Health data, as well as a bunch of other apps and whatnot. You can track nearly everything, and the integration with my healthcare providers’ system is priceless, especially for me as a cancer patient who is seeing doctors and getting bloodwork/vitals done super often. I freaking LOVE this app! I am so stoked about learning all these interesting things about my health and my environment and habits. It’s just so cool.

The only thing I wish it had was integration with the myAir app, so I could track the data from my CPAP machine and get insights about those things. But maybe someday—the devs are pretty great about updating the app and adding new features, so hey, maybe I’ll get lucky! In any case, this is an amazing app and has totally changed my outlook on my health—by sort of gamifying health tracking in a way, it’s encouraged me to be more mindful of my health and the things that impact it, and to do things that are good for me.

reviews.title: Better than any other health app
reviews.text:
It can connect and access a terrifying amount of data - at a time when that definitely is risky and feels costly against the need to insure privacy etc. so buyer beware. But of all the dozens (at least) of ways I have tried to track all of the correlations to the intense pain and symptoms of my autoimmune disease and food and weather- nothing comes close to being as easy and efficient by a mile. I have been consistently tracking for over a month and finally upgraded to track insights. It wasn’t necessary - but it did point out aspects of weather and heart rate correlations I had never considered - and that is valuable if only to point out to me what I have not given attention to. So I give it 4 stars - but this is in part unfair perhaps - because the star subtracted is mostly left off for reasons that are not the fault of the app entirely - like the data exploitation and vulnerability of anyone in the US. If you are someplace with socialized medicine you may feel more comfortable, or someone who’s government doesn’t feel bent towards fascism that is deeply tied to data farming and exploitation than you are probably less anxious than me about the caveats. The app clearly needs the data to perform - so perhaps a clear, straightforward explanation of how it is being anonymized in detail - and how it’s is not lumped and dumped on a server but rather distributed into different encrypted sets or some other reassurance would do a lot to reassure me.

One request for developers - and this is made with the clear appeal to also not change anything else because it is absolutely perfect otherwise (seriously! It’s brilliant!) 
If symptom groups could be used in insights that would be hugely helpful. It is bothersome to try and look for correlations one symptom at a time when you have a lot of- but the groups related to specific conditions might even shed more light on actual correlations. I have thought about adding a super category as a symptom and going back to crunch a sort of median - but it actually seems like a fair simple programming addition that would make a huge different to many users. Thanks in advance! 

And regarding the cost. It is fair- with the amount I sink into supplements and co-pays the value of this app stands out as actually providing a huge amount of benefit for the cost. If I ran a clinic, I would provide it to patients. My ability to self report medication adherence is fairly bad - but the app, if used, can give an exact record - in addition to trillions of other benefits. There is a lot of power in the data - and in this way I think it should stay entirely in the hands of the patients, but this will benefit everyone by empowering them to communicate more in detail and provide informed observations (in a quantified format that Dr.’s can refer to over time) to their practitioners.

reviews.title: amazing app for chronic illness
reviews.text:
this app is amazing! for context, i am chronically ill and i have a variety of symptoms. i use data from my fitbit primarily

Guava does a lot of what many other apps do, like help me track when i take my meds and remind me to take them. but it goes above and beyond with things like the insights. it’s told me correlations between things like weather changes and my heart rate, which has helped me look into a few symptoms and better manage them. i had no idea that certain things affected me so much, and Guava helped me focus on what to prioritize for better health. it shares correlations that it finds, but also lets you look at any correlation you want to investigate and change the settings of how it categorizes a significant change.

also, when my doctors upload my blood work i can see it right away. it shows me my results in a way that’s really easy to understand, because they show what average good / bad results are and where my results fall on that color coded spectrum. a few times in the ER, it’s helped me process my results before the doctor even returns to tell me. a lot of the time my doctors had said “all labs look good” but with Guava, i was able to see that i was consistently low in one area which lets me follow up with the specialist for that issue. having the context right there with my labs makes them way easier to understand, before i used to have to look everything up.

another thing i like is their preparation feature. it helps me prepare for an upcoming appointment and mark down what i want to discuss. sometimes it’s months between certain specialist visits, so having an ongoing log of what symptoms i want to discuss AND the data is really helpful to have in one place.

they also have these tabs that make it way easy to log regular things, like my group of morning meds. you just tap your phone to the tab and it adds them in for you. i am not very good at manually logging in stuff so, the extra help is great! it means i have better data to understand my health and health changes. when i next need to start a new medicine, i would love to tab it in so i can see all the data and how it really affects my health.

they also have a great team. guava is made by chronically ill women who care about their product, and have personal experience dealing with health issues. it shows in the thoughtfulness of the app, and the new features they’ve integrated since i’ve had it. Also, when i first got it i was flaring really bad and very brain foggy. i messaged their account on insta and they helped me figure it all out. Then, they started making more tutorial videos. it’s amazing how thoughtful they are and how much they value community input.

reviews.title: Got chronic illnesses? You need this app.
reviews.text: I’ve been chronically ill since I was tiny, with my life turning upside down at 10. By my teen years, I had the giant three-ring binder most of us who’ve had to advocate for our health have lugged around to doctor’s appointments to carry all of our lab results, x-rays, chart notes, you name it. But we’re in the digital age now and though I’ve tried other apps and services that have kept track of a couple different things, none have covered them all— that is, until Guava came along. This app is truly all-encompassing and the seamless integration with a whole host of patient portals makes compiling all your information in one place a breeze. Within three minutes of installing Guava, I had records SINCE THE DATE OF MY BIRTH  in the app, right up to my vitals at my last doctor’s appointment a couple weeks before. There are a lot of features I haven’t had a chance to try yet but I’m stoked just to see that they’re options— insights, planning for doctor’s appointments ahead of time to maximise your visit, logging your medications… this app is amazing and may just be the resource I’ve been looking for to finally retire that old binder. Thank you, Guava!

reviews.title: Subscribed on day one
reviews.text:
I just started using this app, partly because I've been trying apps like it for my stomach issues, but I recently broke out in hives which has never happened. 

Searched the app store since I didn't currently have a tracking app and found this one. 

After logging the last 3 days worth of hives into the symptom tracker, and browsing around the info I imported from my medical record, I subscribed on that first day. 

Amazing features that are beautifully implemented and I can't WAIT to dive into correlations once I have more data logged. 

Seems incredibly full featured, and I feel like some apps don't understand how I want to view my data and its patterns, but this app feels like they truly understand why I am tracking all this stuff and what info I want to get out of it. 

I honestly never write app reviews, even if I hated an app, but this one just has me so excited that I have found such a useful app with an affordable subscription. 

I really hate when devs make these sort of apps insanely and prohibitively expensive. It's like they act like they want to help people but then ask for $300 a year. But this app is very reasonably priced for all the features it offers.

reviews.title: Has Absolutely Everything (on the Free Version!)
reviews.text:
I’ve been trying out different health trackers for a while, and they all have 1-2 things they excel at while everything else falls behind. I think Guava is finally what I’ve been looking for.

It connects to devices, Apple Health, and most of my patient portals. It tracks appointments, medications, symptoms (with body “heat maps”!) measurements, and more. It lets you add custom categories, entries, events, and more which is great for my weirder symptoms and specific triggers. It’s great for data nerds like me!

My favorite part is that everything you need is available with the free version! The premium subscription has some great features, but it’s mostly advanced insights and easier transfers from doctor’s notes. All the tracking and analysis features I need I can get for free. 

My one request is that I wish it had more advanced analysis to do with length of symptoms. I have chronic headaches, and while there is a way to put a start and end time in my log, there’s not any good way to see what affects the length of my headaches (or the average length or anything like it). Regardless, Guava is a great app and I’m so glad I found it.

-can add in factors that may be cause, not just symptoms. Such as medications and when they are taken, drinking caffeine, eating a certain type of food. 

App is useful for:
-possible correlation/causation of symptoms (Do I have a food allergy?)
-trends in symptoms (is my headache always only in the morning?)
-monitoring pre-existing conditions (diabetes, migraines)
-monitoring medication side effects (Is my pain medication making me nauseous?)

reviews.title: Life changing- amazing app and developers!
reviews.text:
I’ve been using guava for almost six months. After a long time of wondering “would it make things easier?” I finally caved and just decided to try it. This is your sign - go ahead and just try it. 

First of all, the app can be comfortably used at the completely free setting. I’d love to get premium when I’m in a place that I can reasonably do that - because I want to support the team behind this amazing resource - but right now, using the basic free setting, I barely notice that there are features I could be paying for. (If I did pay for them, I’m sure I’d see many benefits, but they’re not too in your face if you don’t have them.)

The other part that really appeals to me is it’s super easy to add functionality as you go. I keep changing the meds that I log, modifying how I track symptoms, and adjusting what is important to me in the app. Granted, I’ll get the most long-term benefits with consistency, but adding things and changing as I go ensures that my use of the app is truly based on my current health and needs. 

Finally, the peace of mind that I get with this app is unbeatable. I’ve done so many “test correlations” to see if there are relationships between different symptoms and triggers I have - and it’s so validating to be able to have an explanation and know what I might be able to change for better results. (Using this app got me to finally increase my water intake to where I’ve been recommended, through tracking that intake and seeing that I wasn’t drinking enough!)
Tracking my migraines (on meds that I thought were the best yet) I was able to show myself that they were more severe than I thought and I switched meds to something that (so far, based on my tracking in Guava) is better! The app gives me tools to advocate for myself through my own medical history. 

If you’re unsure, give it a try. Like me, you’ll probably love it.

reviews.text:
This app is an absolute game changer trying to track my developing chronic illnesses and working with multiple doctors and specialties. 

Favorite features:

- can make categories to track (I made trackers for shower and bath, to track how long they were, what temp, what activity (full shower, shave, body only, etc) to try and track against symptoms and flares because POTS is wild)
- tags within each tracked category because I have to be SO granular
- records for allergies, med list, dr contacts, past test results, procedures
- can link to healthcare portals to auto import charts and visit notes (sometimes I see more info there than what is shown on the actual portal)
- biomarkers page to compare your blood work results over time all together, it’s incredible, it’s how I saw my TSH fluctuate over the years when doctors never saw a specific result being problematic, but the overall trend was)
- the insights tab to try and track correlations is a great start. It’s still in beta and I’m still trying to find my habit of logging to get some results and experiment in there. My problem is I have so much happening in my body daily that it’s hard for me to truly record everything so I’d record maybe 25-30% of a flare day

Wishlist/improvements🙏🏻:
- food is entered manually still, would be amazing (if possible) to code in a food scanner for barcodes to search or a way to input cal or track macros, that stuff can still affect flares and such like not getting enough protein, and not realizing it. I don’t personally need a calorie counter in this type of app, but I do find myself flipping to another app to be able to count my macros and calories and make sure I’m getting enough sustenance.

reviews.title: Such a helpful app!
reviews.text:
I downloaded this app at a friends recommendation and I am so happy I did! I love having all my records in one place, it makes it so easy to keep track of everything. Not only that, but I find it such a helpful tool to track health conditions and see correlations and information I would never know without the app. I feel so much more knowledgeable about my own health. 

There are so many features I am still discovering and I cannot wait to explore more. It is perfect for day to day tracking as well as long term records. I love it!

reviews.title: The app that changed my life
reviews.text:
I could go on for hours about how amazing and user friendly guava is, but as someone who is chronically Ill and faces disability, I want to focus on how since this app has launched, I have achieved remission of some conditions, the best mental and physical health I’ve experienced in years, and the security of knowing my health is so important to an app/company. 

Guava is like MyChart on steroids, and allows me to combine my medical info from multiple entities (like my PCP, specialists, Quest, even my Fitbit (although many other smart devices achieve the same benefits)). I’ve lost weight, found a healthy diet not just for how my body looks, but how it feels, identified issues in my sleep schedule, and helped make adjustments in my overall routine. With Guava, I’ve been able to work with my doctors to choose the right medication and therapy plans. It encourages me even when I feel defeated. 

I’m finally achieving the possibility of normalcy I never knew possible. No app or doctor or treatment has been able to make it so accessible to someone who is young and often wants to so badly avoid my symptoms//treating them in a desperate attempt at normalcy. It’s hard to focus so much on things like taking medicine consistently and timely twice a day, but guava and their notifications have finally helped me achieve routine medicine intake and the outcomes are indescribable.

In combination with mychart, healthcare has never felt more manageable or effective. I have even received test results faster with guava many times. Their correlation aspect  has helped improve my health and lifestyle, and the constant hard work of their team//willingness to receive feedback means a lot to those with disability and chronic illness, especially when doctors don’t always have the time to individualize information and feedback like guava does.

I have never been more adamant about an app or healthcare platform, and I hope guava changes others’ lives and healthcare as it has mine. 

THANK YOU GUAVA!!!!!

reviews.title: Guava is great!!
reviews.text: I’ve been using Guava for a couple months now and it’s been super helpful! I use it for almost all my health needs like cycle tracking, record storage, symptom logging, and more. The correlating feature lets me compare my health across all boards (which most apps with correlations can’t do). Download!!

reviews.title: Essential app to have on my homescreen
reviews.text: The Guava health app makes it so accessible to keep track of health information - from uploading my vaccine card, to inputting various health metrics, and even integrating seamlessly with my Garmin - I feel on top of my health because I can access vital data all in one place with just a few taps! Huge shoutout to the Guava team.

reviews.title: Beat way to see all of your medical data
reviews.text: With compatibility with the VA, I’m very impressed.  The developers have taken genuine care in development and safety of your data.  Even my doctor was impressed. Works with Apple Watch data too….a game changer for sure.

reviews.title: organizes for you
reviews.text: love having something to organize all my health stuff for me and see combined charts of all my labs. uploaded my big stack of old lab records and now they're digitized into charts. also helps to easily see whether I'm being "healthy" according to national guidelines, and whether my daughter is on track for her vaccines.

reviews.title: Love this! All my records in one place.
reviews.text: Finally an app that consolidates all my medical records in one easy to use platform. I don’t have to jump around multiple portals that use different formats. I can easily access data using search words, dates, topics or facilities. The Guava QR coded Emergency Card and the custom metric tracking options make this site even more valuable.

reviews.title: Game changer
reviews.text: This app is great.  It lets me show my doctor the labs and X-rays I already had done so I don’t have to repeat them.  It also lets me track some symptoms I’ve been dealing with for the past 18 months.  The correlation feature is helping me see if my activity or caffeine or alcohol intake is impacting these symptoms.  Soooo much easier than trying to track all that on paper and bring to my doctor visit!  Super easy to work with.  I love this app!

reviews.title: Helpful and informative
reviews.text: My daughter showed me this app and urged me to download it. I like that it has all of the data I care about, I even got a Fitbit so I could better track my sleep from guava. What I like most, though, is that it shows me where I’m out of range of normal for my age. It’s reassuring to know I have all of my most accurate and up to date records on me at all times. It gives me peace of mind knowing that I also have the guava card, which emts can scan in case of emergency. At my age, it’s a real concern that there could be a delay in care. So I like this card.

reviews.title: All my info in 1 place
reviews.text: It’s pretty cool to have all my fitness device data, patient portal data and logged data in 1 place. I didn’t realize how uncommon that was until I started looking around for apps. With guava, I can see my medical records from my patient portals, my sleep and steps data from my Fitness devices (I go back and forth between Apple Watch and Fitbit and guava logs them both), and the stuff I care about tracking, like my mood, alcohol and caffeine that I manually enter. I’ve actually been changing some of my habits to improve my Guava score, which is such a neat feature! On top of all of that, I love my guava card. I show it to pretty much everyone I know. Very cool.

reviews.title: Changed my life and my skin!
reviews.text: Been trying to figure out how my skin has been behaving to the various acne meds I’ve been prescribed by my dermatologist to figure out which ones work the best. I’ve tried so many and it’s helpful to have a log of what caused allergic reactions, what made me sensitive and what didn’t work at all.  This app has been a life saver for tracking my skin journey and I’ve finally found a routine that works for my acne!
